system_prompt: You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.
a1_answer:
DESIGN: Dual-mode pressure detection system with continuous flow impedance monitoring

USER CONSTRAINT: No more than 1 nuisance alarm per 14 days (rationale: maintains patient compliance while ensuring safety)
USER CONSTRAINT: Detect complete occlusion within 15 minutes (rationale: prevents dangerous hyperglycemia events)
USER CONSTRAINT: Detect partial occlusions (>20% delivery deficit) within 2 hours (rationale: addresses slow leaks that current system misses)
USER CONSTRAINT: No change to wearable form factor (rationale: preserves patient acceptance and comfort)

CALCULATED: Primary pressure threshold at 25 psi (rationale: maintains existing sensitivity for complete blockages while reducing false positives)
CALCULATED: Secondary impedance threshold at 15% baseline resistance (rationale: detects partial occlusions before they reach pressure threshold)
ASSUMPTION: Baseline impedance established during priming phase (rationale: provides reference point for detecting deviations)

FALSIFICATION TEST: Simulate partial occlusions (20-40% flow reduction) across 100 pumps in ambulatory conditions with varying patient activities (sitting, walking, sleeping) and environmental conditions (temperature, humidity). Measure time to alarm and record false positive rate. Test passes if 100% of partial occlusions are detected within 2 hours and nuisance alarms remain below 1 per 14 days.
